best_for: Windows users who make short screen recordings for bug reports, docs or tutorials and want to trim and annotate frames before saving a GIF or video.
description:
ScreenToGif is a screen recorder and animation editor written by Nicke Manarin and shared as open source under the Microsoft Public License. It is made for short clips, where every frame counts.

While recording, you can drag the hollow capture window onto another window to snap it to that size, and set the frame rate anywhere from 1 to 60 frames per second. In the editor you can delete duplicate frames, drop frames at a set interval to shrink the file, reverse the clip or make it play forward and back, change how long each frame stays on screen, crop and resize, and add captions or title frames. Most of these actions have keyboard shortcuts.

points.title: Record, then edit frame by frame
points.text: It records a part of the screen, a webcam, or a sketchboard you draw on. The built-in editor then lets you work on the recording before you save it.

points.title: More than GIF
points.text: Recordings save as GIF, APNG, video, PSD or PNG images. Recent releases fetch the latest FFmpeg through the plugins page or the installer.

points.title: Needs .NET 9
points.text: The app requires the .NET 9 Desktop Runtime or newer, so install that first if the app will not start.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: It is MS-PL licensed with no price. The author takes donations through PayPal, Patreon and Ko-fi.

points.title: Install options
points.text: This page lists machine-wide MSI installers and MSIX packages for x86, x64 and Arm64; the MSIX needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later. Portable zips and a Microsoft Store version are on the project's pages.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version. The listing here keeps 45 versions.
